cases.question_text: Describe an energy transfer when a finger presses a piano key, naming the starting and receiving objects.
cases.model_response: Kinetic energy passes from the moving finger to the key, causing the key to move.
criteria: Identifies finger as source and key as receiver

cases.question_text: Explain a transformation when a piano’s vibrating mechanism produces sound.
cases.model_response: Mechanical kinetic energy associated with vibration is transformed into sound energy that travels through the air.

cases.question_text: Describe the transfer when moving air turns a wind turbine’s blades.
cases.model_response: Energy is transferred from the moving air to the blades, which gain kinetic energy.

cases.question_text: Explain the useful transformation when a rotating turbine drives a generator.
cases.model_response: Kinetic energy of the rotating mechanism is transformed into electrical energy by the generator.

cases.question_text: Explain the useful energy transformation while a rechargeable battery is charging.
cases.model_response: Electrical energy supplied to the battery increases its stored chemical potential energy.

cases.question_text: Describe one transfer after a lamp emits light into a room.
cases.model_response: Light energy travels from the lamp to objects in the room.

cases.question_text: Predict the result of one broken filament in a two-lamp series circuit and explain.
cases.model_response: Both lamps go out because the only path is broken.

cases.question_text: Predict the result of one broken filament in two independent parallel lamp branches with an ideal supply.
cases.model_response: Only the failed branch goes out; the intact branch still has a complete supply path.

cases.question_text: Predict the result of a break in a wire between an ideal battery and both parallel branches.
cases.model_response: Both branches lose sustained current because the break interrupts their shared supply path.

cases.question_text: Two equal resistors are in series across 8 V. Explain their voltage drops.
cases.model_response: Each has 4 V because equal resistances carry the same current and share the 8 V equally.
criteria: Equal resistance and same current justify equal sharing

cases.question_text: Explain why parallel branches at the same voltage can carry unequal currents.
cases.model_response: The branch resistances can differ. I = V/R gives more current in the lower-resistance branch.

cases.question_text: Justify parallel branches for two lamps that need independent control.
cases.model_response: Each branch has its own closed supply path. Opening a switch in one branch does not interrupt the other.

cases.question_text: Evaluate comparing two balls if one is dropped on carpet and the other on wood.
cases.model_response: Ball type and surface both change, so rebound differences cannot be attributed to ball type alone. Use the same surface.

cases.question_text: Evaluate a comparison where one ball is dropped and the other is thrown down.
cases.model_response: Throwing adds kinetic energy, so the initial energy differs beyond the planned factor. Release both from rest.

cases.question_text: Evaluate declaring a ball reliable from a single rebound measurement.
cases.model_response: One result does not reveal variation. Repeat under the same conditions and compare spread as well as the mean.

cases.question_text: Explain why a displaced ruler zero is not fixed by taking more trials.
cases.model_response: The same offset can affect every measurement. Correct the reference level; repeats mainly help assess random variation.

cases.question_text: Evaluate choosing a robot only because it is fastest when it must also remain stable.
cases.model_response: Speed alone ignores the stability requirement. Test both speed and stability against stated criteria.

cases.question_text: Explain why comparing launch speeds of the same car can compare kinetic energy from springs.
cases.model_response: With mass fixed, kinetic energy increases with speed squared. Use the same car and a consistent spring-loading and release protocol.

cases.question_text: Evaluate: “The second lamp gets less current because the first lamp uses it up.” Assume a steady series circuit.
cases.model_response: Current is the same throughout the loop. The lamps transfer electrical energy; they do not consume charge.

cases.question_text: Explain the limitation of calling voltage a force.
cases.model_response: Voltage measures energy transferred per unit charge in J/C; force is measured in newtons. A push analogy is not the definition.

cases.question_text: Evaluate placing an ammeter directly across a battery to measure lamp current.
cases.model_response: An ammeter must be in series with the lamp. Across the battery it can create a low-resistance bypass and excessive current.

cases.question_text: Explain why electron arrows and conventional-current arrows point opposite ways in metal wires.
cases.model_response: Electrons carry negative charge. Conventional current is defined in the direction positive charge would move.

cases.question_text: Explain why “more resistance means less current” needs a condition.
cases.model_response: I = V/R gives that comparison when voltage stays constant. A simultaneous change in voltage can change the result.

cases.question_text: Evaluate: “A battery stores electric current.”
cases.model_response: It stores chemical energy. Current is the rate of charge flow when a circuit operates, not an energy store.
